data.name: Muruga
data.gender_notes: Muruga is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Muruga is the Hindu god of love, war, and victory. He is also known as Subramanya and Kartikeya. He is the son of Shiva and Parvati and is considered the god of war in the epic Ramayana. The name Muruga carries the meaning “God of Love and War” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Tamil, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Muruga usually hope their child will grow to embody god of love and war and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Muruga represents the divine power of love, compassion, and protection. He is also the god of war and victory, symbolizing the power to overcome obstacles and challenges in life.
data.etymology: Muruga belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Love and War.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muruga total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Muruga is a major deity in the Shaiva, Shakti, and Saivism traditions of Hinduism. He is revered and worshipped across India, particularly in Tamil Nadu, and is also popular in Nepal and Sri Lanka. Muruga is depicted as having two cars, a peacock and a horse, and is also associated with the eight-faced goddess Maya and his brother Ganesha. The annual festival of "Skanda Shashthi" is dedicated to Muruga, which is celebrated with great enthusiasm and devotion in various parts of India and other countries.
data.spiritual_significance: Muruga is believed to be the embodiment of perfection, compassion, and love. He represents the triumph of good over evil and is a symbol of hope, strength, and salvation. In Hindu mythology, Muruga is said to have slain the demon Surapadman, thus ridding the world of evil. He is also the giver of boons, and is believed to grant the wishes of those who seek him in sincerity and devotion. Muruga's teachings emphasize the importance of love, devotion, and surrender to God, as well as the importance of inner purity and self-discipline. Thus, Muruga's name carries a profound spiritual significance, reminding us to remain focused on our inner journey towards self-realization and divine connection.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Muruga, the god of love and war, symbolizes the inner struggle between our desires and spiritual growth. His name, meaning 'reddish-complexioned one,' represents the awakening of our inner warrior to conquer worldly passions and attain divine love.

historical_references.reference: Muruga is believed to be an early Dravidian deity, possibly dating back to the Neolithic age. He is mentioned in the ancient Tamil texts, such as the Tirumurai and the Purananuru.
historical_references.time_period: Neolithic age to Early Common Era
historical_references.context: Ancient Tamil texts and early Dravidian religious practices.

historical_references.reference: Muruga is also associated with the Chola Dynasty (9th to 13th centuries CE) and is depicted as a warrior god, often shown riding a peacock and holding a spear. The Chola temples at Thanjavur and GangaiKondaCholapuram are famous for their intricate carvings of Muruga and his consort, Deivayanai.

modern_usage.modern_context: Muruga, also known as Kartikeya or Subramanya, is a major deity in the Hindu religion, particularly venerated in the southern Indian states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. In modern contexts, Muruga's devotionalism has gained significant popularity among the youth, especially through social media platforms such as Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok. On Instagram, there are numerous accounts dedicated to Muruga and his temples, with millions of followers sharing prayers, devotional images, and stories. On YouTube, there are scores of devotional channels providing Muruga's hymns, puja procedures, and other spiritual content. TikTok has also become a popular platform for sharing brief devotional videos, prayers, and stories related to Muruga. The transnational following of Muruga can be seen through the establishment of temples and communities in various parts of the world, such as the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, and Singapore.
